page: Microsoft Azure DC16as_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD processor and managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is allocated 16 dedicated virtual CPUs, offering dedicated core scheduling without fractional CPU sharing. The memory subsystem provides 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a consistent 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with the GPU count configured at zero.

Storage architecture for the DC16as_v6 is diskless with respect to local media, listing no local storage capacity. Instead, the virtual machine relies on network-attached storage architectures and is rated as Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with managed enterprise disk volumes. Networking provisions include zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual network routing or external IP allocation.

Because the instance lacks local scratch space or ephemeral disks, all persistent file operations must traverse the network storage layer, making performance dependent on the attached volume tiers. The hardware configuration provides solid compute and memory density for standard enterprise deployments. DC16as_v6 is best suited for application servers, containerized microservices clusters, middle-tier enterprise backends, and relational databases operating on networked block storage.

Without local solid-state drives, disk operations depend entirely on network-attached storage throughput and IOPS limits. With its balanced resource configuration, the DC16as_v6 provides stable compute capacity for multi-threaded applications, enterprise web backends, microservice deployments, intermediate caching systems, and database engines that rely on remote managed block storage.
